qs_053:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for a cap table audit ahead of a fundraise. The goal of this step is to gather and organize all investor-related documents so ownership, board consents, and investor rights can be verified.

Please ask me for the following if not already provided: (1) where our company documents are stored (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox, a data room tool, or local files) and access details using my configured credentials, (2) the name of our cap table management tool if we use one, and (3) a list of known investors/rounds so you can check completeness.

Once you have access, locate and compile the following documents for every financing round and investor: stock purchase agreements, convertible notes or SAFEs, board consent resolutions approving each issuance, stockholder/investor rights agreements (information rights, pro-rata rights, voting agreements), option grant agreements and the option pool ledger, any warrants, and current capitalization table exports. Organize these into a single folder structure or index (by round, then by document type) so they can be cross-referenced against the cap table.

As you go, flag any gaps: missing signatures, missing board consents, rounds with no corresponding agreement, or investors listed on the cap table without supporting documents. Produce a checklist noting which documents are present, which are missing, and which need human review for accuracy or legal interpretation.

When done, report back with: a summary of documents found and organized, the folder/index structure created, a list of gaps or missing items flagged for follow-up, and any documents whose validity or completeness you're unsure about. Do not attempt to interpret legal sufficiency or sign anything — this remains a human step for legal review.

qs_053:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a cap table accuracy audit ahead of a fundraise. I will provide (ask me if missing): (1) the current cap table file (spreadsheet or export from our cap table management tool), (2) a folder or repository location containing signed source documents — stock certificates, SAFEs, convertible notes, option grants/exercise agreements, board consents authorizing issuances, and any warrant agreements, and (3) my company domain/name for labeling outputs.

Please do the following:
1. Parse the cap table into a structured list of every stockholder/holder, security type, number of shares/units, issue date, and price/valuation cap or discount where applicable.
2. Go through the source documents folder and extract the same fields (holder name, security type, quantity, date, key terms) from each signed document.
3. Cross-reference each cap table line item against its corresponding source document, flagging: missing documents, quantity mismatches, missing board consent for an issuance, missing signatures, or terms (e.g., liquidation preference, pro-rata rights, vesting schedule) present in the document but not reflected on the cap table.
4. Produce a discrepancy report organized by holder, listing each flagged item, the cap table value, the document value, and the document link/filename for reference.
5. Note any documents you could not locate or open, and any holders on the cap table with no matching document found.

Do not judge whether discrepancies are material or make corrections to the cap table yourself — compile findings only. Once the discrepancy report and document cross-reference are complete, stop for human sign-off so I can review materiality and decide on corrections before the raise. Report back with the discrepancy report, a summary count of clean vs. flagged entries, and the list of missing/unmatched documents.

qs_053:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a board consent review as part of a cap table audit before a fundraise. I need you to organize and index all board consent/resolution documents so I can personally judge completeness and validity — you will not make legal judgments yourself.

First, ask me for: (1) where our corporate records live (e.g., a shared drive, cap table platform, or document repository, and how you can access it with my configured credentials), (2) the current cap table export or equity issuance list (option grants, SAFEs, convertible notes, stock purchases, founder shares), and (3) any known date range or entity name to scope the search.

Then: locate every board consent, written resolution, or meeting minute related to equity issuances, option pool increases, officer/director appointments, and investor rights grants. For each equity issuance line in the cap table, attempt to match it to a corresponding board consent document. Build a table with columns: issuance/grant (recipient, security type, date, amount), matching board consent found (yes/no/partial), consent date, and file location/link. Flag any issuances with no matching consent, consents missing signatures or dates, or consents that reference the wrong terms (e.g., mismatched share counts or prices).

Summarize your findings as a checklist: total issuances reviewed, count fully documented, count missing or incomplete, and a list of specific gaps needing my attention (e.g., "Series A investor rights consent — no signature page found").

Do not decide whether any consent is legally sufficient or complete — that judgment is mine. Once your index and gap list are ready, stop for human sign-off and present the checklist so I can review each flagged item before we proceed with the audit.

qs_053:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare an attorney sign-off package for our cap table audit ahead of a fundraise. This is a policy-gate step: a licensed attorney must personally review and certify compliance, so you must prepare all materials and then stop for human sign-off — do not certify, approve, sign, or submit anything on my behalf, and do not contact the attorney directly unless I've given you their email and asked you to send the draft.

First, ask me for anything missing: (1) location/link to our current cap table file, (2) board consent records, (3) investor rights documents (e.g., ROFR, pro-rata, information rights agreements), (4) any prior legal review notes, (5) the name/firm and contact info of the attorney handling sign-off, and (6) our target raise timeline.

Once you have these, do the following:
1. Compile a concise audit packet: current ownership summary (founders, investors, option pool, convertibles/SAFEs), a list of board consents with dates and links, and a summary of investor rights by security class.
2. Flag any gaps or inconsistencies you notice (e.g., missing signatures, undocumented grants, mismatched share counts) in a clearly labeled 'Open Questions for Counsel' section.
3. Draft a short cover email to the attorney summarizing the raise context, attaching/linking the packet, and requesting written sign-off confirming the cap table and instruments comply with applicable securities and corporate law.
4. Save the packet and draft email in a shared location I specify, and give me a checklist of what's included and what still needs my input.

Since this is an async, human-approval step, note that the attorney's response will arrive later — tell me how you'll track/poll for their reply if I ask you to check back, but do not proceed with any cap table changes until I confirm the attorney has signed off. Report back with the packet summary, flagged issues, and draft email for my review.
